key_insight: Higher-order parity constraints can improve QAOA success beyond connectivity benefits, with simulations suggesting faster correlation propagation as the mechanism.
engineering_relevance: Parity-based QAOA offers a hardware-demonstrated route to better optimization outcomes on sparse graphs using parameters trained on smaller instances.
method: Apply selected parity transformations to Signed Max-Cut on 3-regular graphs.
Classically optimize QAOA parameters on training instances with up to 14 vertices.
Transfer parameters to larger instances on IBM Heron processors and apply error mitigation.
evidence_signal: Across the tested 40-vertex instances, parity-based QAOA with error mitigation identified optimal solutions in every case, while conventional QAOA did not under the same conditions.
watch_item: Results are limited to the tested instances and hardware conditions; broader scalability and the implementation cost of higher-order operators remain concerns.
paper_title: Higher-order Parity Constraints for Quantum Approximate Optimization
